note: One narrow idea per Short. Public-domain book; hooks and examples in our own modern words.

chapters.title: Part 1: What you are, what you have, what you seem

episodes.title: Three kinds of wealth
episodes.hook: There are three kinds of wealth. Most people chase the weakest one.
episodes.angle: What you are (health, mind) matters more than what you have, and both matter more than reputation. Example: a rich man with a bored mind versus a poor reader with a rich one.

episodes.title: Health first
episodes.hook: A healthy beggar is happier than a sick king.
episodes.angle: Without health no other good counts. Example: someone who sacrifices sleep for money, then spends the money on doctors.

episodes.title: The boring rich
episodes.hook: Money can't fix an empty head.
episodes.angle: An inner life protects you from boredom better than wealth. Example: the lottery winner who's bored within a year.

episodes.title: Opinions are poison
episodes.hook: You worry what people think. They barely think of you.
episodes.angle: Valuing others' opinion is a madness that causes much unhappiness. Example: changing outfits three times for people who won't remember it.

episodes.title: Pride vs vanity
episodes.hook: Pride lives inside you. Vanity lives in other people's eyes.
episodes.angle: Pride is internal and stable; vanity depends on applause. Example: two musicians, one who plays for himself and one who checks views.

episodes.title: Politeness is a mask
episodes.hook: Politeness is an air cushion. Empty, but it softens every bump.
episodes.angle: Courtesy costs little and avoids pointless conflict. Example: holding the door for someone you don't like.

episodes.title: Don't show your hand
episodes.hook: Tell your friend nothing you'd hide from your enemy.
episodes.angle: Secrets can turn against you; be careful what you share. Example: the group chat screenshot that went public.

episodes.title: Love being alone
episodes.hook: If you can't enjoy being alone, you'll accept bad company.
episodes.angle: Those who can't bear solitude tolerate anyone. Example: staying in a draining friendship because the alternative is a quiet Friday.

episodes.title: Smart people need less company
episodes.hook: The richer your mind, the less you need other people to fill it.
episodes.angle: A full inner life makes solitude a pleasure, not a punishment. Example: a kid content building Lego alone for hours.

episodes.title: The porcupines
episodes.hook: Why do people who get close always end up hurting each other?
episodes.angle: Like porcupines in winter, people need warmth but get pricked when too close; politeness is the right distance. Example: roommates who were best friends until they lived together.

episodes.title: Avoid pain, don't chase pleasure
episodes.hook: Stop chasing happiness. Start avoiding misery.
episodes.angle: A wise person aims at a painless life, not a thrilling one. Example: the person who skips one wild night to avoid three bad days.

episodes.title: Want less
episodes.hook: Every new desire is a new way to be unhappy.
episodes.angle: Our happiness depends on the ratio between what we want and what we get. Example: someone happy with an old phone until he sees the new model.

episodes.title: Boredom and pain
episodes.hook: Life swings between pain and boredom. You decide where you land.
episodes.angle: Need brings pain, comfort brings boredom; a busy mind escapes both. Example: someone who finally gets a free weekend and is miserable by Sunday.

episodes.title: Today is the only day
episodes.hook: This exact day will never come back. Act like it.
episodes.angle: Value the present instead of chasing the future. Example: a parent on a phone at the park while the kid looks for them.
